glossary.definition: — The amount of computation performed relative to data movement.
— A bounded mechanism by which a downstream stage limits upstream production.
— Combining memory activity from nearby GPU threads into efficient memory transactions when access patterns permit it.
— A deliberately inspectable implementation used to define expected semantics independently of an optimized GPU path.
— The time by which a unit of work must complete according to a stated requirement.
— In CUDA terminology, a GPU or other CUDA-capable execution target controlled by host code.
— A condition in which threads executing together follow different control-flow paths, potentially reducing execution efficiency.
— Elapsed time across the complete boundary relevant to the user or system contract, rather than one internal stage.
— Computing that deliberately divides work among processors with different architectures or execution characteristics.
— A CUDA resource and scheduling metric describing active warps relative to architectural limits; it is not a direct measure of useful throughput.
— Host memory arranged to support direct asynchronous transfer behavior required by particular CUDA workflows.
— A system whose correctness includes timing requirements in addition to logical results.
— Single instruction, multiple threads; CUDA's execution model in which threads are grouped for hardware execution while retaining thread-level semantics.
— A CUDA ordering domain for asynchronous operations.
— Completed work per unit time under a stated workload.
— The hardware execution grouping used by NVIDIA GPUs for CUDA threads.
